text: In the 1980s, 101 Dewson Street was a thriving hub of black, gay and lesbian activism in Toronto. The house in Dufferin Grove was the home of writer, editor, and activist Makeda Silvera, who started the Dewson House Collective with her partner Stephanie Martin in 1983, turning the century-old home into a hotbed of activity and organizing. Many important organizations came out of 101 Dewson Street, including Lesbians of Colour and Sister Vision Press. Zami — one of the first organizations in Toronto and Canada specifically for gay and lesbian people of colour — was created around the kitchen table at 101 Dewson by Debbie Douglas, Makeda Silvera, and Douglas Stewart. Zami meetings were held at the 519 Church Street Community Centre and out of 101 Dewson.
